items.title: Nick Brignola interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, July 28, 1997
items.q: my first biggest influence in my life on saxophone was Paul Desmond.

ctx.x: him and he went home and told his father and his father hit him. But the fact that you were playing by ear was not good enough.

Right. And also the material that he was training me to play was not what I wanted to play. So I used to play with the radio. I would listen — most of the — well you may not have been around them, but most of the band leaders back then played clarinet. It was Benny Goodman, Artie Shaw, Jimmy Dorsey, Woody Herman. Clarinet was all over the place. So I used to just play along with the radio. And most of the pop music of the day was the big band music. So that’s what I grew up on. I learned a million tunes — not…
Can I wind back just for a second?

items.title: Nick Brignola interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, July 28, 1997
items.q: MR. Alto first? That is from school?

ctx.x: Yeah, you have a nice write-up in the Grove, actually, I don’t know if you’ve seen it but it’s very nice. Also in, there’s a big compilation that just came out of many, many jazz CD’s and you’re in there with some nice reviews of your work.
Ah. That I wasn’t aware of. MR. Alto first? That is from school?
You want to go right from the beginning?
